title: Retirement security is a present social contract with a 2032 institutional deadline
source_unit: Congressional Budget Office, CBO's 2026 Long-Term Projections for Social Security, September 17, 2026
geography: United States; Social Security program, Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund, current-law 75-year projection

financing_gap.value: the gap between Social Security outlays and revenues generally widens over the next 75 years

mechanism.value: A long-horizon financing imbalance becomes a present expectation problem when workers, retirees and institutions must interpret what unchanged law can credibly promise

observations.method: CBO annual projection of Social Security revenues and outlays for the next 75 years under generally unchanged current law; this record uses the official report page and its summary of the linked workbook.
observations.uncertainty: The projection is conditional on current-law assumptions and is not a forecast of enacted policy, household behavior, political response or lived retirement adequacy.
observations.subgroup: Current workers paying payroll taxes, current and future retirees, survivors, dependents, employers and households making work, saving and care decisions around expected public retirement income.
observations.counterinterpretation: A widening projected gap does not by itself establish an imminent loss of benefits, a particular reform, or a uniform burden across generations; those outcomes depend on future law and distributional choices.

observations.period: Fiscal year 2032; Old-Age and Survivors Insurance Trust Fund

deadline.unit: fiscal year in which CBO projects the OASI Trust Fund balance is exhausted

visibility.value: A specific institutional date makes retirement-system solvency legible as a near-term political and household-planning issue rather than an abstract 75-year chart

policy_choice.value: The source establishes the exhaustion projection but does not specify the post-exhaustion benefit, financing or reform outcome

observations.method: CBO official summary of the 2026 long-term Social Security projections.
observations.uncertainty: Trust-fund exhaustion is conditional on the report's current-law projection and should not be read as a claim that a specific automatic benefit reduction or payment outcome will occur.
observations.subgroup: People approaching retirement, younger workers assessing the credibility of future benefits, families coordinating paid work and unpaid care, and political constituencies assigning responsibility for reform.
observations.counterinterpretation: The date can mobilize reform and planning without producing a single shared public narrative; perceived urgency may differ by age, income, health, family support and trust in institutions.

observations.period: Long-run intergenerational frame; current workers, retirees and dependents

intergenerational_link.value: Payroll-financed retirement expectations connect work, aging, family care, public revenue and political voice across generations

legitimacy_question.value: The practical question becomes whether the system is experienced as reliable, fairly financed and responsive before the projected deadline arrives

consumer_social_effect.value: Expected public retirement security can shape saving, labor-force timing, family transfers, care arrangements and willingness to accept tax or benefit changes

observations.method: Interpretive extension of the CBO projection, explicitly separated from the report's measured fiscal projections.
observations.uncertainty: The CBO source does not measure public attitudes, saving behavior, family care, consumption, political attribution or subgroup-specific adequacy; those require linked survey, administrative and episode evidence.
observations.subgroup: Workers, retirees, caregivers, employers, taxpayers and households with unequal access to private savings, housing wealth, health and family support.
observations.counterinterpretation: Public retirement systems can retain legitimacy through reform, trust, private resources or strong family support; a fiscal projection alone cannot establish cultural conflict or political realignment.

related_sources.claim: Official CBO report page with publication date, 75-year current-law scope, widening outlay-revenue gap and projected OASI Trust Fund exhaustion in fiscal year 2032.
Official data workbook linked by CBO for the projections underlying the report.

boundary: This record identifies a retirement-security, intergenerational-contract and institutional-legitimacy subtheme from a conditional CBO projection. It does not establish post-2032 benefit levels, automatic benefit reductions, reform choices, public opinion, household adequacy, saving behavior, family care, political response or causal effects; those require linked policy, survey, household and episode evidence.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official CBO report page was reviewed for the September 17, 2026 publication date, 75-year current-law projection scope, widening outlay-revenue gap and projected fiscal-year-2032 OASI Trust Fund exhaustion; the linked workbook was identified but exact workbook bytes were not used for numeric extraction.
